# hands/requests

what people asked Teeny to build, and which one it picked.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/requests <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): pick; skip; self; vote-open
- Job (writes state or calls the core): none
- Operator only (never call): reset ID [--note T]
- Read only: list [--status S] [--max N]; get ID; prices; vote

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `list [--status S] [--max N]` | R | The requests, newest first (20), optionally one status: `pending`, `picked`, `skipped`, `shipped`, `failed`. |
| `get ID` | R | One request and its ledger (`build_request_events`: when, which verb, the status it moved to, the note). |
| `pick` | A | `{id, reason}`. |
| `skip` | A | `{id, reason}`. |
| `self` | A | `{text}`. |
| `reset ID [--note T]` | O | Back to `pending`, whatever it was, with the old status in the ledger. |
| `prices` | R | What a paid build request costs and how to pay (frozen, `evals/prices.toml`). |
| `vote` | R | The weekly vote (`teeny_hands/votes.py`): the latest one, `open` with the count so far, or its `result`; and `next_pick`, the winner `pick` must take, while it is still pending. |
| `vote-open` | A | `{text, options}`: posts a vote on 2 to 4 pending requests through `hands/x post` (guard, posting rules, `DRY_RUN`), open for 7 days. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `get`, `list`, `pick`, `prices`, `reset`, `self`, `skip`, `vote`, `vote-open`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--max`, `--note`, `--status`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `hands/requests <verb> --help` (never put a VAR= in front of a command: the shell refuses it, and DRY_RUN is not yours to set). The full account is in docs/hands.md.
